reviews.review:
Ich habe wenig erwartet und bin positiv überrascht worden.

Ja, es gibt einige Bugs und ja die Animationen in den Dialogen sind Schrott, aber die Story ist (bisher) gut und es kommt das klassische Mass Effect Gefühl auf. Endlich auch mal wieder ein Spiel, das nicht nach 20h durch ist.

Fans von ME sollten auf jeden Fall zugreifen, der Rest wartet evtl. lieber auf nen Sale.
Would love to have played this, shame the game doesn't load properly. Third party platform Origin is involved and I'm kind of pissed that can't play. Seems like a cool game though.

Even as a fan of the original triglogy, I held off for a long, long time before giving this game a try.
I was mostly pleasently surprised. I completed most of the campaign and its sidequests with around 71 hours of playtime.

TL:DR: It's a good game and sometimes even among peak ME experiences. There are still a good number of bugs and inconviences, but not enough for me to not enjoy the game.

+ no need of background knowledge from past ME titles necessary. It's a fresh start and the Codex has a good amount of background information on races, technologies
+ the Heleus Cluster is huge
+ story is a tad generic but at least it's handled enthusiastically
+ tons of content
+ planets are pretty big, with dozens of sidequests to find, and there is enough variation in the locales as well.
+ still a Masterclass in dialogue writing
+ humor is intact
+ mostly good voice acting. I disliked the female Ryder's voice early on, but as she grew more confident progressing through the story, I liked her more and more.
+ Likable companions
+ companion banter when driving around with the Nomad
+ very fluid combat and buffed enemy numbers compared to earlier entries
+ highly customizable playstyle; you're can freely choose your skills, profiles and weapons, however switching and changing in missions is finicky since you only have a limited number of ability slots and profile system can't be changed on the fly. Weapon weight still affects your ability recharge time.
+ some of the best missions in all of ME
+ looks good, even if many assets are being reused
+ choices do matter in the end (well, for the most part, some where left out for future entries that may or may not come after the launch disaster of ME:A)
+ story itself is conclusive but left room for DLC / future entries. Since I was satisfied with the note the game ended on, I am not weighing this as negative.
+ you can finish up sidequests after the main story line, although depending on your choices, some content may not be available.
+ loading times are hidden beneath neat animations (approaching planets can thankfully be skipped). Running on SSD, I had little to no noticeable loading stops.
+ there is modsupport for this game which can take care of some of the negative points of the game (eg Shut up SAM)

- The game has still a huge amount of bugs as of 2020
 -> got yeeted off of the Nomad twice in the middle of nowhere
 -> got yeeted to the main menu twice
 -> had to reload a number of times to make a quest or door trigger work
 -> had an unimportant sidequest bug out after dieing that even reloading wouldn't fix (enemies wouldn't spawn)
 -> mostly early game, some dialogue animations clip through geometry, characters flipping into position
 -> A few conversation triggers aren't properly cleaned up so they duplicate when running through them.
- some dialogues still suffer from dead staring NPCs
- SAM is the new Navi. An option to turn off its informal blaring about hazards and minerals would have been welcome
- at least one unmarked sidequest has stuff in places that you cannot visit afterwards
- The menus have a lot of trouble keeping up with everything that's going on.
 -> Inventory management is... okayish, but could have benefitted from a filtering system in addition to categorization
 -> Each time you open the journal you have to backtrack through like 4 menus, and the quest log can't keep up with the amount of quests sometimes. Unmarked Quests are tracked through additional tasks and just clutter up everything.
- Research & Development is a nightmare, as is most of the economy behind it. Unless you know what to go after, you will probably waste a lot of Research Points and then not have enough to build what you actually want. Research Points are scarce, and each level of research costs additional points that you still have to research even after reaching a higher tier of research. You will most likely only ever use a handful of guns and try out other stuff you find. Also, building and refitting your modded guns to a higher equipment tier is a literal stupid given how unintuitive it is.
- Mass Effect still can't do good Boss fights. Most just throw a buff random dude with a ton of ads at you.
- The game got a little too easy for me in the final missions, playing on the 2nd highest difficulty mode. That perception may change depending on class and abilitiy choices, companions and personal playstyle, of course.
- Some of the backtracking from side quests is just too much, especially if you do not run this game on an SSD and have to endure the loading times

Many of the negative points can be overlooked since you will only spend a couple of minutes in the menus once you know your way around. Loading times were usually short.
My main complains are SAM which is just taking too prominent a roles and blares over banter and sometimes even mission critical information with its informal talk of minable minerals and hazard information, to the point it became annoying. OoT Navi annoying and beyond.
The other thing that I categorize as a big detracting negative is how buggy the game still is. The amount of reloads due to malfunctioning triggers even in a 70 hours campaign is inexcusable and definitely detracts from enjoying the game.
Despite that, I thoroughly enjoyed my time with the game even if it doesn't spark the same amount of passion that the original trilogy did.

Recommendation for people who like RPG / Action titles, (semi) open worlds, exploration and character interaction, but you might want to wait for a sale.
combat is fun. story is ok. if you new to the mass effect series then get it ig but comparing this to the mass effect trilogy, its a sad dissapointment.

Edit: After completing the game, I can say that it was definitely worth my money. I keep comparing this to the first Mass Effect game, and how if you were to play that one on its own, it really kind of sucked. It's a shame that Andromeda got kind of dumped and won't be getting any more lore/content into its trilogy (Quarian ark anyone?) Although with the unnamed fifth Mass Effect game being announced, there may yet be hope for some more Andromeda lore. Only time will tell if this becomes another ME1, or the dying breath of a failed trilogy.



As a game, it really runs beautifully, especially if you have the computer oopmh to crank everything up to ultra (and especially if you have an HDR monitor). Sadly, it really just can't hold a torch to the original trilogy. The storytelling in this game is fairly poor, but it definitely could be worse. You'll find yourself spamming spacebar in many dialogues simply because they're completely meaningless. 

Really, the reason I continue to play the game is because the actual game mechanics are so well fleshed out. Combat in this game is leaps and bounds ahead of the OT, and it's genuinely a fun game to play, even if I want to wring my neck every time I have to go get another fetch quest from a bland character.


P.S. If you happen to have an RGB keyboard with game synchronization, ME:A has quite literally the best lighting synchronization I've ever seen implemented in a game. Definitely not a reason to buy the game, just saying that more devs should do this. Your "lit" keys change between combat and non-combat modes, only lighting up the keys you need. Abilities are red, and have the breathing effect when on cooldown. Just awesome to notice the small things.

Cons:
1.Repetitive mission design; mostly fetch quests 
2.Loyalty missions do not impact the overall ending of the game
3.Inferior dialog options; no renegade or paragon
4.Characters are carbon copy of the original mass effect; namely mass effect 1
Pros:
1.Visual presentation is top notch, take planets such as Elaaden or Havarl as good examples
2.Combat is fast paced and has lots of versatility to it; the ability to change class mid combat is a nice touch although your powers would need to cool down after you have selected a class
3.Some cool dialog between characters when you are driving the nomad( this game's version of the original mako) 
in conclusion I would say a decent enough game if you want to sink some hours in but don't come in looking for something amazing.
